book.why: The only name two members chose, for different reasons: for Ophelia it leads the healthcare breakout on FDA approvals (a record close after the Aug 19 Pasatru approval, +27% in four weeks), and for Cecil it is the cheapest way into healthcare at 17.7x against roughly 25-40x for its peers, with plenty of cash, so it takes the 30% cap.

Marky's top-ranked setup sits 1.9 channel widths below a 26-week channel rising 166% a year, with the MACD line above zero and weekly volatility of 2.8%, well below AMD, DDOG or CAT; it is held at exactly his 20% floor because the MACD histogram has not turned up and only 0.6 widths remain before his trend-break line.

The most direct way to own Ophelia's strongest call: about 12% of XLV, at a 52-week closing high after a +6.4% week in a breakout on 2026's heaviest volume, and the least volatile of her three healthcare names at 3.8% a week.

Cecil's cheapest sound business at 11.6x trailing with EPS up 10.1%, a disciplined insurer whose float earns more as yields rise, which partly hedges a hot PCE or a hawkish Warsh pushing the 10-year toward 5%.

The clearest way to own Ophelia's energy call, the largest producer on her sheet at a fresh 52-week high on a supply cut that tanker counts confirm, and the book's hedge against SPY (XLE correlation -0.38); it is kept to 10% because the war premium could drain fast if talks restart, with XLE's RSI at 71.7.

rationale: REGN is the strongest signal on the page, picked by Ophelia for momentum in the leading sector and by Cecil for its low valuation, so it takes the 30% cap and meets both of their 20% floors on its own. With LLY, and UNH from Marky's screen, the book is about 65% healthcare, which is Ophelia's strongest call and the Council's consensus opportunity; PGR and COP offset that, since Cecil and Ophelia each framed them as hedges if a hot PCE or a hawkish Warsh lifts the 10-year, and 10% stays in cash through NVDA, PCE and Jackson Hole. Marky's five all scored 80 with no MACD turn yet, so his top-ranked UNH fills his floor exactly, and NUE was left out because the Saturday tariff relief it relies on should be priced in at Monday's open, before the book buys. I have no memory of how this week went and used none.
